daily_reality.summary: Prosthodontists evaluate patients' oral health, design and fabricate dental prostheses (crowns, bridges, dentures, implant-supported restorations), and perform complex restorative procedures. They work in private practices, academic settings, and hospital dental departments.
typical_tasks: Examine patients and assess oral health needs for prosthetic restoration
Take impressions and measurements using face bows, dental articulators, and intraoral scanners
Design and fabricate dental prostheses (crowns, bridges, dentures, implant-supported prostheses)
Place and adjust permanent fixtures including implant-supported restorations
Fit removable prostheses (complete/partial dentures) with adjustments
Collaborate with dental technicians and lab workers on prosthesis fabrication
Consult with general dentists and other specialists on complex cases
Perform digital workflow tasks using CAD/CAM systems
Maintain patient records and process insurance documentation
key_documents: Patient treatment plans and consent forms
Dental prosthesis prescriptions and lab orders
Referral letters to/from general dentists and specialists
CE documentation and board certification records

deadlines.emergency_cases: Same-day for dental trauma or acute prosthetic failure
deadlines.lab_fabrication: 1-3 weeks typical turnaround for custom prostheses
deadlines.insurance_claims: Within 30-90 days of service depending on payer
deadlines.ce_requirements: 125 CE credits every 5 years for board certification

daily_reality.seasonality: Relatively stable year-round. Slight increase in elective cosmetic procedures before holidays and summer. Insurance-driven rush at year-end as patients use remaining benefits.

regulatory.summary: Prosthodontists must hold a DDS/DMD degree plus 3-year specialty residency. Licensing is state-by-state through state dental boards. Board certification through ABP is voluntary but highly valued. 2026 sees the new Interstate Dental Compact and updated ADA CERP standards.

key_laws.name: State Dental Practice Acts (vary by state)
American Board of Prosthodontics (ABP) Certification
key_laws.status: Active — new alternate pathway for 2026 certification

key_laws.name: ADA CERP Standards Update
key_laws.status: Effective June 2026 — reduced from 14 to 5 standards

requirements: DDS or DMD degree from accredited dental school
National Board Dental Examination (NBDE) or INBDE
Continuing education (varies by state, typically 20-40 hours/year)
Board certification through ABP (voluntary but recommended)

regulatory.penalties: Practicing without a license: varies by state — misdemeanor to felony charges, fines up to $10,000+, loss of license. HIPAA violations: $100-$50,000 per incident. Malpractice claims average $200K+ settlements in dental specialties.
controlling_bodies: American Board of Prosthodontics (ABP — voluntary certification)
American Dental Association (ADA — standards and CE accreditation)

tools.summary: Prosthodontists heavily rely on CAD/CAM digital workflow, intraoral scanners, CBCT imaging, and practice management software. Digital dentistry is now standard with nearly all labs using CAD/CAM.

primary_tools.name: Intraoral Scanners (iTero, 3Shape TRIOS, Medit)
primary_tools.description: Digital impressions replacing traditional molds — standard in modern prosthodontic practice

primary_tools.name: CAD/CAM Milling Systems (CEREC, exocad, 3Shape)
primary_tools.description: Computer-aided design and manufacturing for crowns, bridges, inlays, onlays, and full-arch prostheses

primary_tools.name: CBCT Imaging (Cone Beam CT)
primary_tools.description: 3D diagnostic imaging for implant planning and complex case assessment

primary_tools.name: 3D Printers (surgical guides, temporary prostheses)
primary_tools.description: Additive manufacturing for surgical guides, models, and temporary restorations

primary_tools.name: Practice Management Software (Dentrix, Eaglesoft, Open Dental)
primary_tools.description: Patient scheduling, billing, insurance claims, and EHR management

secondary_tools: Digital Smile Design (DSD) software for cosmetic planning
Dental implant planning software (Nobel Clinician, BlueSkyPlan)
pain_points: High cost of CAD/CAM equipment ($100K-$200K+ investment)
Interoperability issues between different digital systems and file formats
Learning curve for digital workflows — transitioning from analog
Insurance reimbursement not keeping pace with cost of advanced materials
Lab communication challenges in digital workflow handoffs

terminology.summary: Prosthodontics uses standardized terminology from the Glossary of Prosthodontic Terms (GPT-10, 2023), combined with dental abbreviations and clinical jargon.

terms.implant-supported: Prosthesis anchored to dental implants rather than natural teeth
terms.abutment: Connector piece between dental implant and prosthetic crown
terms.occlusion: How upper and lower teeth come together (bite relationship)
terms.edentulous: Having no natural teeth (complete tooth loss)
terms.full-arch: Prosthesis replacing all teeth in upper or lower jaw
terms.zirconia: High-strength ceramic material used for crowns and frameworks
terms.e.max: Lithium disilicate ceramic — popular for aesthetic restorations
terms.prep: Tooth preparation — shaping tooth to receive a crown or veneer
terms.impression: Mold of teeth/oral structures for fabricating prostheses
terms.GPT: Glossary of Prosthodontic Terms (official terminology reference)

career_psychology.summary: Long training path (11+ years) but among the highest-earning dental specialties ($216K-$429K). Rewarding specialty with visible patient transformations. Relatively small specialty with ~3,500 active prosthodontists in the US.
career_path: Dental school — DDS or DMD (4 years)
Board Certification through ABP (optional but prestigious)
Academic faculty / Program Director / Department Chair
fears: Malpractice lawsuits from prosthetic failures or complications
High student debt ($300K-$500K average for dental school + residency)
Technology becoming obsolete quickly — constant need to upgrade
Competition from general dentists doing more prosthodontic work
motivation: Transformative impact on patients' quality of life (eating, speaking, confidence)
Intellectual challenge of complex treatment planning
Blend of art and science in prosthesis design
Growing demand driven by aging population and implant awareness
burnout_factors: Extremely long training pathway (11+ years before independent practice)
High student debt burden relative to starting salary
Precision-demanding work with no margin for error
Insurance administrative burden and reimbursement battles
Isolation — small specialty with few peers in most practice settings

community.summary: Active professional community centered around the American College of Prosthodontists (ACP) and American Prosthodontic Society (APS), with multiple annual conferences and growing digital presence.

associations.name: American Prosthodontic Society (APS)
associations.type: Scientific society focused on prosthodontic education

events: ACP Annual Session (October, major national conference)
ICP — International College of Prosthodontists conferences
online_communities: Facebook groups for prosthodontists and dental implant professionals

market.summary: Strong and growing demand for prosthodontists driven by aging population, implant awareness, and digital dentistry adoption. Over 1,200 current job openings. Salary $216K-$429K with top earners exceeding $429K.

job_outlook.demand_drivers: Aging population, implant technology adoption, cosmetic awareness

market_trends: Digital dentistry and CAD/CAM becoming universal in prosthodontic practice
Interstate Dental Compact enabling easier multi-state practice
Nanotechnology and smart materials emerging in denture fabrication
Growing patient demand for aesthetic and implant-based restorations
ADA CERP simplification (June 2026) reducing CE compliance burden
